data.title: mRNA Translation
data.statement:
A messenger RNA (mRNA) is a sequence of nucleotides ({{A}}, {{C}}, {{G}}, and {{U}}). Your cells use mRNA to build <<amino acid>> chains by reading groups of {{3}} nucleotides called <<codons>>, from <<left to right>>, as follows:

• The mRNA is first scanned for the <<start codon>>, {{AUG}}.
• If found, the mRNA is translated <<codon by codon>>, beginning with the start codon. Each codon encodes for a specific amino acid, and these amino acids are chained together in the same order as their codons.
• Translation stops when one of the <<stop codons>> ({{UAG}}, {{UAA}}, {{UGA}}) is translated, even if there are more nucleotides left in the mRNA sequence. This termination forms a proper amino acid chain that is later folded into a protein.

Given an mRNA sequence:
• If no start codon exists, output {{NONE}}.
• Else, if no stop codon exists, output {{ELIMINATE}} (abnormal translation).
• Else, output its proper amino acid sequence after translation, including {{STOP}} for the stop codon.

<<Example>>
```mRNA:  A G U C G A U G G U G A G U U G A C U A A U G A A
codon:           |___| |___| |___| |___|
                  AUG   GUG   AGU   UGA
amino:            Met   Val   Ser   STOP```

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A messenger RNA (mRNA) is a sequence of nucleotides (A, C, G, and U). Your cells use mRNA to build amino acid chains by reading groups of 3 nucleotides called codons, from left to right, as follows:

• The mRNA is first scanned for the start codon, AUG.
• If found, the mRNA is translated codon by codon, beginning with the start codon. Each codon encodes for a specific amino acid, and these amino acids are chained together in the same order as their codons.
• Translation stops when one of the stop codons (UAG, UAA, UGA) is translated, even if there are more nucleotides left in the mRNA sequence. This termination forms a proper amino acid chain that is later folded into a protein.

Given an mRNA sequence:
• If no start codon exists, output NONE.
• Else, if no stop codon exists, output ELIMINATE (abnormal translation).
• Else, output its proper amino acid sequence after translation, including STOP for the stop codon.

Example
mRNA:  A G U C G A U G G U G A G U U G A C U A A U G A A
codon:           |___| |___| |___| |___|
                  AUG   GUG   AGU   UGA
amino:            Met   Val   Ser   STOP





   

      
Input

      
Line 1: A string, h, consisting of all 64 space-separated codonCombinations, each in the format, codon:amino_acid, representing a codon and the amino acid it codes for.
Line 2: A string, s, of nucleotides (individual letters) beginning with 5' Cap (m7Gppp) and ending with a Poly-A Tail (AAAA...).

   

   

      
Output

      
Line 1: The protein sequence with each amino acid (each element) separated by a space, from Met to STOP. If there is no sequence, output NONE. If the sequence is abnormal and has no stop codon, output ELIMINATE.

   

   

      
Constraints

      
7<= codonCombination <= 8
Each codon is a sequence of exactly 3 nucleotides (A, C, G, and U).
amino acid is either STOP or a 3-letter sequence

0 < length of s < 1000
s will only contain the 4 listed nucleotides (A, C, G, and U), apart from the 5' cap and poly-A tail

   

   

      
Example

      

         

            
Input

            
UUU:Phe UUC:Phe UUA:Leu UUG:Leu UCU:Ser UCC:Ser UCA:Ser UCG:Ser UAU:Tyr UAC:Tyr UAA:STOP UAG:STOP UGU:Cys UGC:Cys UGA:STOP UGG:Trp CUU:Leu CUC:Leu CUA:Leu CUG:Leu CCU:Pro CCC:Pro CCA:Pro CCG:Pro CAU:His CAC:His CAA:Gln CAG:Gln CGU:Arg CGC:Arg CGA:Arg CGG:Arg AUU:Ile AUC:Ile AUA:Ile AUG:Met ACU:Thr ACC:Thr ACA:Thr ACG:Thr AAU:Asn AAC:Asn AAA:Lys AAG:Lys AGU:Ser AGC:Ser AGA:Arg AGG:Arg GUU:Val GUC:Val GUA:Val GUG:Val GCU:Ala GCC:Ala GCA:Ala GCG:Ala GAU:Asp GAC:Asp GAA:Glu GAG:Glu GGU:Gly GGC:Gly GGA:Gly GGG:Gly
m7GpppGGCAUAAUGUUUGCACUGAAAGGGUAUCCCGUAUAACCGAUCAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA

         

         

            
Output
